Amongst the runners were Ranjit Bhatia, on his last outing from Wimbledon before returning home, Jack Brown, recently returned from Cyprus and already re-establishing himself as a danger man and Cliff Roffey, home on furlough from Kenya.

Cliff Roffey who was spending a few weeks in England on furlough from Kenya, and who had regained the form he showed when with us regularly, was on the 10th stage, and with a fine performance shattered the Valley opposition and took us back to 2nd place, 67 secs behind Portsmouth.

The exception was Jack Brown, now running with much of the fire shown in his pre-Cyprus days, who moved up to 1st place on the fourth of the six stages. Taking over from Cliff Roffey in 3rd place, he soon put St. Albans behind him and moved steadily up to Woodford.

Stephen's College, Delhi; and Cliff Roffey, who ran so well in the "Brighton" is now back in Kenya for another 3 year tour of duty. Talking of the "Brighton", what a heartening sight it was to see Jack Brown handing over to Ron Linstead!
Cliff Roffey arrived in this country a few weeks ago for a spot of leave from business in Kenya. I saw Cliff before the Club '10' and he said he did not feel as fit as on his last visit.
A most welcome competitor was Cliff Roffey, home on a spell of leave from Kenya, whose sun-tanned form was decidedly out of character with the surroundings.

CLIFF ROFFEY is now living at Kericho in Kenya where he is working as an accountant for Brooke Bond Liebig Kenya Ltd.
